title: Physical quantities and units

parts.text:
32 Which two units are used to define the coulomb?
A
ampere and second
B
ampere and volt
C
volt and ohm
D
volt and second

hints: Notice the coulomb is the unit of electric charge $Q$, so look for the equation that defines charge.
Recall how electric current $I$ is defined as rate of flow of charge: $I = Q/t$.
Rearrange to $Q = It$ and check what units current and time have to make the unit of $Q$.
walkthrough: Identify the quantity: the coulomb $\text{C}$ is the SI unit of electric charge $Q$.
State the defining relation for current: current is charge per unit time, $I = Q/t$.
Insert units: unit of $I$ is ampere $\text{A}$ and unit of $t$ is second $\text{s}$, so unit of $Q$ is $\text{A s}$.
Therefore $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$, so the coulomb is defined using ampere and second. This is option A.

A.explanation: Charge is current multiplied by time, so $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A} \times 1 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: Volt is the unit of potential difference, and $\text{ampere} \times \text{volt}$ gives power in watt, not charge.

C.explanation: $\text{volt}$ divided by $\text{ohm}$ gives current in ampere by $I = V/R$, not charge in coulomb.

D.explanation: $\text{volt} \times \text{second}$ gives magnetic flux in weber, not charge.
